newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: 43 Lebanese freed by Zaire rebels reach SAfrica.
newsitem.headline: 43 Lebanese freed by Zaire rebels reach SAfrica.

text.p: A group of 43 Lebanese nationals, released by Zaire rebels after nearly a month of captivity in the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi, arrived in South Africa, Lebanon's ambassador said on Monday.

"The group of 43 people arrived at Johannesburg International airport on Sunday night via Lubumbashi. They were not allowed to leave Mbuji mine since April 4," ambassador Charbel Stephan told Reuters.
He said a few members of the group of mainly men had been hospitalised in Johannesburg "due to stress". Thirteen left South Africa on Monday on two flights for Beirut, he added.
Lebanon's Minister of Emigrants Talal Arslan said on Sunday that the rebels had released 46 Lebanese nationals. Stephan insisted that only 43 were freed.
Stephan said the group was captured by the rebels in the chaos during the takeover of Mbuji-Mayi from government forces.
He said the homes and offices of the Lebanese businessmen, mainly diamond buyers, had been ransacked by soldiers. "They lost everything," he added.
He said the group was released after direct intervention by the United Nations and the South African government.
